a181a22a746f241e.summary: Smart-ring data from 23,000 adults across 5 months proves irregular sleep timing spikes depression and loneliness even with 8 hours sleep. Hook: 'Going to bed at different times every night is secretly wrecking your mental health.'
a181a22a746f241e.notes:
- Study: 23,000 adults tracked over 5 continuous months using smart-ring biometric sensors.
- Finding: High sleep-wake timing variability (bedtime shifting by >60 mins) correlates with severe spikes in depression, anxiety, and feelings of social isolation.
- Crucial detail: The mental health disruption occurred regardless of whether individuals got 7-8 hours total sleep—circadian misalignment alone drives the effect.
- Practical habit: Anchor wake-up time within a 30-minute window every day of the week, including weekends.
